alt: A timeline marks when a text is set (what the characters know) and when it was written (what the audience knows), with the gap between them often deliberate. In the example, An Inspector Calls is set in 1912, when Birling calls the Titanic unsinkable, but was written after the Second World War for an audience who knew it sank. Chips list other contexts: class, gender, race, migration and identity.
caption: The gap between setting and writing gives the audience knowledge the characters lack.

caption: Four chosen moments from opening to ending, each serving one argument.

alt: Three stages of the model paragraph on Mr Birling. AO2: the word unsinkable creates dramatic irony. AO1: being wrong about the Titanic makes the audience doubt his other claims. AO3: the gap between setting in 1912 and writing after the Second World War exposes his selfish individualism.
caption: A short quotation, a method, an interpretation and context that explains the choice.
